Fusilli alla Molisana

Fresh fusilli with Molise-style lamb, veal, sausage, tomato, red wine, Pecorino, and parsley ragù.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 3/5 lb fresh fusilli
about 1/4 lb lamb breast
about 1/3 lb veal
1 large fresh pork sausage plus one-third of a second sausage
2 cups chopped peeled tomatoes
1/4 cup plus 2 tsp red wine
2/3 onion, finely chopped
2/3 carrot, finely chopped
2/3 celery stalk, finely chopped
3 tbsp plus 2 tsp extra-virgin olive oil
2/3 cup finely grated Pecorino
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/4 tsp dried chile
3/4 tsp fine salt

For cooking the fusilli
3 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat.

2. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for about 10 minutes.

3. Cut the lamb and veal into small pieces.

4. Add the lamb, veal, and sausage with the casing removed and meat crumbled.

5. Brown for 8–10 minutes, turning and breaking up the meat.

6. Pour in the red wine and cook for 3 minutes.

7. Add the tomatoes and fine salt.

8. Cover with the lid slightly ajar and cook over low heat for about 2 hours, stirring every 20 minutes.

9. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

10. Cook the fresh fusilli until al dente.

11. Drain and immediately dress with the ragù.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and finish with the Pecorino and parsley. Serve the chile at the table or divide it evenly among the portions.

Chef's note

The lamb, veal, and sausage need a long gentle simmer so all three meats integrate into the tomato while retaining their texture.

Rustic durum-wheat sagne with beans, tomato, and onion-carrot-celery soffritto.

Eggless sagne retain a rustic bite and absorb the bean-and-tomato sauce well during the brief final toss.

Ditalini with cannellini beans, mussels, cherry tomatoes, garlic, chile, parsley, and crisp prosciutto.

about 7/16 lb ditalini

1. Clean the mussels thoroughly, removing the beards and shell buildup.

2. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a wide skillet. Add the mussels, cover, and cook for 4–5 minutes, removing them as they open.

10. Drain the pasta and transfer it to the saucepan.

11. Finish cooking for 3 minutes, gradually adding the full 1/2 cup warm water while stirring continuously.

12. Add the mussels and heat for 1 minute.

13. In a dry nonstick skillet, cook the diced prosciutto for 3–4 minutes, until lightly crisp.

Service

Divide the pasta and beans among 4 bowls. Finish with mussels in their shells, crisp prosciutto, and the remaining parsley.

Chef's note

The strained mussel liquid directly seasons the beans and pasta, so the amount of additional salt is deliberately moderate.

Taccozze and Beans

Molise-style taccozze with borlotti beans, pork rind, cherry tomatoes, onion, chile, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the taccozze
2 1/2 cups type 00 flour
2/3 cup water
2/3 tsp fine salt

For the sauce
1 1/4 cups dried borlotti beans
1/3 lb cleaned pork rind
1 onion, finely chopped
1 1/3 cups halved cherry tomatoes
4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus 1 tbsp for finishing
1 chile
1 tsp fine salt

For soaking and cooking the beans
6 1/3 cups water for soaking
6 1/3 cups fresh water for cooking

Preparation

1. Rinse the borlotti and soak them in the cold water for 12 hours.

2. Drain and transfer the beans to a pot with the fresh water and pork rind.

3. Bring to a gentle boil and cook for 90 minutes, until the beans are tender and the pork rind is soft.

4. Add 2/3 teaspoon salt during the final 15 minutes. Reserve all of the broth.

5. Make the taccozze by combining the flour and salt. Add the water and knead for 10 minutes.

6. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

7. Roll the dough to about 1/16 inch thick and cut into irregular diamonds.

8. Heat 4 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan. Add the onion and chile and cook for 5 minutes.

9. Add the cherry tomatoes and remaining salt and cook for 5 minutes.

10. Add the beans, pork rind cut into pieces, and 3 cups plus 3 tablespoons of the bean broth.

11. Bring to a boil and add the taccozze.

12. Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is done.

Service

Divide among 4 bowls and finish with the remaining 1 tablespoon raw olive oil.

Chef's note

The taccozze cook directly in the bean-and-pork-rind broth, allowing the pasta starch to thicken the soup naturally.

Cavatelli with Ventricina

Handmade cavatelli with ventricina sausage ragù, tomato, bay leaf, and Caciocavallo.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the cavatelli
2 1/3 cups durum-wheat flour
3/4 cup warm water
1/2 tsp fine salt

For the ragù
1 1/4 cups tomato sauce
1/3 lb ventricina, cut into small pieces
2/3 cup finely grated Caciocavallo

1 bay leaf
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

For cooking the cavatelli
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Mound the flour on the work surface and add the salt.

2. Gradually add the warm water and knead for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

3. Cover with a damp kitchen towel and rest for 20 minutes.

4. Divide the dough into small portions and roll into ropes about 3/8 inch thick.

5. Cut into pieces 3/4–1 inch long.

6. Drag each piece across the work surface with your index and middle fingers to create the characteristic hollow.

7. Arrange the cavatelli on a floured tray.

8. Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan.

9. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.

10. Add the bay leaf and ventricina and cook for 4 minutes, until the ventricina begins to render its fat.

11. Add the tomato sauce, salt, and pepper.

12. Cover partially and cook over low heat for about 40 minutes.

13. Remove the bay leaf.

14. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

15. Cook the cavatelli for 7–10 minutes.

16. Drain and transfer to the ragù. Toss for 1 minute.

17. Turn off the heat and add the Caciocavallo.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and serve immediately.

Chef's note

Let the ventricina render some of its fat before the tomato is added so its spices and flavor spread evenly through the ragù.

Lasagna Beneventana

Benevento-style lasagna with tomato sauce, tiny meatballs, Neapolitan salami, fiordilatte, hard-boiled eggs, and Parmigiano.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the tomato sauce
6 cups tomato passata
1 small yellow onion, finely chopped
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 cup water

For the tiny meatballs
2/3 lb ground beef
2 cups loosely packed stale bread pieces
1 cup water for soaking the bread
1/2 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1 large egg
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil for browning
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For assembly
about 9/16 lb egg lasagna sheets
1 1/8 lb fiordilatte, cut into strips and thoroughly drained
about 7/16 lb Neapolitan salami, diced
1 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
4 large eggs
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Make the sauce. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan, add the onion, and cook for 6 minutes.

2. Add the passata, water, and salt. Cover partially and cook over low heat for about 1 hour.

3. Spread the fiordilatte over paper towels and let it drain.

4. Soak the stale bread in the water for 5 minutes, then squeeze it very dry.

5. Mix the bread, beef, Parmigiano, egg, parsley, salt, and pepper.

6. Form small meatballs about 5/8 inch in diameter.

7. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the meatballs in batches for 3–4 minutes. Drain and reserve.

8. Boil the 4 eggs for 9 minutes. Cool, peel, and crumble coarsely.

9. Dice the salami.

10. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

11. Spread a thin layer of sauce over the bottom of a roughly 8×12-inch baking dish.

12. Alternate lasagna sheets, sauce, meatballs, salami, fiordilatte, hard-boiled eggs, and Parmigiano to create about 6 layers.

13. Finish with pasta, sauce, Parmigiano, fiordilatte, and black pepper.

14. Bake for 25–30 minutes.

15. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Service

Cut into 6 portions and serve hot.

Chef's note

Drain the fiordilatte thoroughly before assembly so the lasagna does not release excess water during baking.

Pasta alla Genovese

Neapolitan ziti with long-cooked golden-onion and beef sauce, white wine, celery, carrot, bay leaf, and grated cheese.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 3/4 lb ziti
about 7 cups thinly sliced yellow onions
1 3/4 lb beef, cut into pieces
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
1/2 cup finely chopped celery, plus a few celery leaves
1/2 cup finely chopped carrot
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 bay leaves
1/4 cup fresh parsley leaves
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
3/4 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano or Caciocavallo

For cooking the pasta
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Slice all of the onions very thinly.

2. Tie the celery leaves, parsley, and bay leaves into a small herb bundle.

3. Heat the olive oil in a very large pot over medium-low heat.

4. Add the celery, carrot, and onions and cook for 8 minutes.

5. Add the salt and herb bundle.

6. Add the beef and brown for 2 minutes.

7. Reduce the heat to very low, cover with the lid slightly ajar, and cook for 2 hours, stirring every 15–20 minutes.

8. Pour in the white wine and continue cooking for another hour, until the onions have completely broken down and the sauce is thick and hazelnut-brown.

9. Remove the herb bundle.

10. Remove the beef, shred it coarsely, and return about half to the sauce. Reserve the rest for serving.

11. Break the ziti into thirds.

12. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil and cook the ziti until al dente.

13. Drain and transfer the pasta to the onion sauce. Toss for 1 minute.

Service

Divide among 4 plates. Finish with the remaining shredded beef, grated cheese, and black pepper.

Chef's note

Neapolitan Genovese is not a tomato sauce. Long cooking transforms the onions into a sweet, brown, creamy sauce that coats the pasta.

Spaghetti with Clams

Neapolitan spaghetti with littleneck clams, garlic, white wine, parsley, extra-virgin olive oil, and chile.

Preparation

1. Soak the clams in the cold salted water for at least 2 hours. Drain and rinse thoroughly.

2. Heat the olive oil in a very wide skillet over medium heat.

3. Add the unpeeled garlic and chile and cook for 1 minute.

4. Add the clams and pour in the white wine.

5. Cover and cook over high heat for 4–5 minutes, removing the clams as they open. Discard any that remain closed.

6. Strain the liquid from the skillet carefully through a fine-mesh strainer.

7. Remove about two-thirds of the clams from their shells and leave the rest in the shell.

8. Return the strained liquid and shelled clams to the skillet. Remove the garlic.

9. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

10. Cook the spaghetti until 2 minutes short of the package's stated cooking time.

11. Drain and transfer directly to the clam liquid.

12. Finish cooking over high heat for 2 minutes, tossing continuously.

13. Add the clams in their shells, parsley, pepper, and fine salt only after tasting the sauce.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and serve immediately.

Chef's note

The strained clam liquid is the core of the sauce. Taste it before adding salt so the finished dish does not become overly salty.

about 1/4 lb fresh sausage, casing removed
1/3 cup finely chopped pancetta
1 medium carrot, finely chopped

Preparation

1. Heat the olive oil in a heavy-bottomed saucepan.

2. Add the carrot, celery, and onion and cook for 10–12 minutes.

3. Add the pancetta and brown for 3 minutes.

4. Add the crumbled sausage and beef.

5. Brown thoroughly for 8–10 minutes.

6. Pour in the red wine and cook for 3 minutes.

7. Add the passata, broth, salt, and pepper.

8. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover with the lid slightly ajar, and cook for at least 2 hours.

9. Stir every 20 minutes and add a little water or broth only if the ragù becomes too dry.

10. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

11. Cook the strozzapreti until al dente.

12. Drain and transfer to the ragù.

13. Toss for 1 minute.

Service

The slow soffritto and thorough browning of the three meats build the flavor before the long tomato simmer.

Ferrara Macaroni Pasticcio

Ferrara sweet-crust pasticcio filled with macaroni, veal-and-beef ragù, mushroom béchamel, Parmigiano, and truffle butter.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

For the sweet pastry
3 3/4 cups flour
14 tbsp cold butter
1/2 cup sugar
2 egg yolks
1/2 tsp fine salt

For the ragù
about 7/16 lb ground veal
about 7/16 lb ground beef
1/3 cup dry white wine
5 1/2 tbsp truffle butter
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the béchamel
1 2/3 cups whole milk
1/2 cup heavy cream
2 tbsp type 00 or all-purpose flour
1 1/2 tbsp butter
1 cup loosely packed dried mushrooms, soaked, drained, and chopped
2 cups finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1/4 tsp freshly grated nutmeg

For the pasta
3/4 lb macaroni or sedanini

For the mold
1 tbsp butter
1 egg yolk for brushing

For cooking the pasta
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Make the ragù. Brown the veal and beef in a dry saucepan over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes.

2. Add the white wine and let it evaporate.

3. Cook for another 10 minutes, until the pan is nearly dry.

4. Add the salt and truffle butter, stir, and remove from the heat.

5. Make the béchamel. Melt the butter, add the flour, and cook for 1 minute.

6. Gradually whisk in the milk.

7. Cook until thickened.

8. Add the salt, pepper, and nutmeg.

9. Turn off the heat and stir in the mushrooms, cream, and Parmigiano.

10. Make the pastry by quickly working together the flour, butter, sugar, yolks, and salt until cohesive, without adding water.

11. Wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

12. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

13. Cook the macaroni very al dente, about 3 minutes less than the package's stated time.

14. Drain and cool slightly.

15. Combine the pasta, ragù, and béchamel while all are lukewarm.

16. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

17. Butter a round baking dish about 12 inches wide.

18. Divide the pastry in two, roll the first disk, and line the bottom and sides.

19. Add the filling in a slight dome.

20. Cover with the second pastry disk and seal the edges firmly.

21. Decorate with scraps if desired and brush with egg yolk.

22. Bake for 30 minutes, until the crust is golden.

23. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Service

Cut into 8 portions and serve hot.

Chef's note

The contrast between the lightly sweet pastry and savory filling defines Ferrara pasticcio. The pasta, ragù, and béchamel should be lukewarm before assembly.

Baked Bolognese Tortellini

Tortellini baked with Bolognese ragù, béchamel, provola, and Parmigiano.

Yield: 5 servings

Ingredients

For the ragù
1 1/8 lb ground beef
about 1/2 lb pancetta, diced
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp tomato passata
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp vegetable broth
1 cup dry white wine
1 carrot, finely chopped
1 celery stalk, finely chopped
1 onion, finely chopped
1 1/4 tsp fine salt

For the bake
1 1/8 lb tortellini filled with Mortadella Bologna
about 2 cups diced provola or scamorza
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp béchamel
3/4 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1 tbsp butter for the baking dish

Preparation

1. Put the pancetta in a cold nonstick skillet and cook over medium heat for 6–8 minutes.

2. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 8 minutes.

3. Transfer everything to a large pot, add the beef, and cook for about 20 minutes, until the liquid evaporates and the meat is well browned.

4. Pour in the white wine and cook for 3 minutes.

5. Add the passata, broth, and salt.

6. Cover with the lid slightly ajar and cook over low heat for at least 4 hours, stirring every 30 minutes.

7. Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil.

8. Cook the tortellini for about half their normal cooking time, around 2 minutes.

9. Drain and combine in a bowl with the ragù and béchamel.

10. Add the diced provola and fold gently.

11. Butter a baking dish and transfer in the tortellini.

12. Cover with Parmigiano.

13. Bake in a preheated 425°F oven for 15 minutes.

14. Broil for 2 minutes, until well browned on top.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and divide into 5 portions.

Chef's note

The tortellini should go into the oven very al dente because they finish cooking in the ragù and béchamel.
